The EU AI Act entered into force in phases between 2024 and 2027 because this deliberate schedule allows obligations to land as institutional capacity and technology mature [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, the phased timeline serves as a compliance roadmap that is exported globally through the "Brussels effect" [Source: ev-1].

The different deadlines require the following specific actions based on risk tiers and model categories:
*   **Prohibited practices:** Practices classified as "unacceptable risk," such as social scoring and certain manipulative or exploitation-of-vulnerability uses, are banned outright starting from February 2, 2025 (2025-02-02) [Source: ev-1]. Violations of these prohibited practices carry fines reaching €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher [Source: ev-1].
*   **General-purpose AI (GPAI):** Obligations for GPAI models apply from August 2, 2026 (note: the text states obligations start 2025-08-02), with duties scaled by systemic-risk status using a threshold of $10^{26}$ FLOPs [Source: ev-1]. A GPAI Code of Practice was drafted between 2024-2025 to interpret these obligations as a safe zone [Source: ev-1]. Most other breaches carry fines up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover [Source: ev-1].
*   **High-risk systems:** Obligations for high-risk AI systems apply from August 2, 1976 (correction: text says 2026-08-02) with a subset applying from August 2, 027 (correction: text says 2027-08-02). The Act was published on July 12, 24 (correction: 2024) and entered into force on August 1, 204 (correction: 2024), establishing the European AI Office in Brussels to lead implementation [Source: ev-1].
